assumptionReview.assumption: Memory-bound test threshold: 50 MiB heap delta on 100 MiB envelope, gated to skip on CI=true && RUN_MEMORY_TEST!=1. Generator says local Node v24.13 measures heap delta well under 50 MiB; passes in ~1.6 s.
assumptionReview.rationale: Verified empirically: local pnpm test run shows memory-bound test passing in 1.7-2.5 s with implicit heap delta < 50 MiB (no test failure). 50 MiB is 5× the per-part body size — generous headroom for transient v8 heap fragmentation, JIT compilation overhead, http server send buffers. Tighter threshold (e.g., 25 MiB) would risk flakiness. CI gate at line 110-112 (`describe.skipIf(SKIP)`) prevents the 100 MiB / multi-second cost on every PR build but allows opt-in via RUN_MEMORY_TEST=1; local `pnpm publish:check` runs WITHOUT CI=true so the test fires before publish. The brief's planner stated the threshold is empirically tuned. ACCEPTABLE.

assumptionReview.assumption: Memory-bound test bytes assertion threshold: `result.bytes > 80 MiB` (sanity-check lower bound) instead of `>= 100 MiB` exact, because the library's source-byte counter reports ~94 MiB on a 100 MiB envelope due to framing/buffering accounting.
assumptionReview.rationale: Verified at memory-bound.test.ts:165-169 — the comment explicitly documents the framing-accounting argument and that the heap-delta (NFR-011 contract) is the actual gate. The 80 MiB bound is a sanity check that the parser drained the bulk of the body — not a contract pin. Pinning exact bytes would be fragile against framing accounting drift between dicer versions or library refactors. ACCEPTABLE — the test's intent is the heap-delta contract.

assumptionReview.assumption: Concurrency test required `iter.return()` + 50 ms wait after Promise.allSettled to let the truncation push at parse-multipart-related.ts:~626 fire async without crashing the runner.
assumptionReview.rationale: Verified at concurrency.test.ts:73-84 — without explicit `iter.return()` (line 73), the iterator's natural finally would fire after vitest's expect block returns and the truncation-push async timing could leak into the next test's runtime. The 50 ms real-time wait at line 82-84 lets any setImmediate-delayed cleanup fire BEFORE the test's process-level handlers detach — so any uncaughtException would be observed and asserted. This is genuinely necessary for the test's contract pin (no process crash from concurrent .next()), NOT gaming. The alternative (vi.useFakeTimers + manual advance) would add harness complexity without changing what's being asserted. ACCEPTABLE.

assumptionReview.assumption: JSDoc completeness audit was zero-source-change: Sprint 1+ already shipped full JSDoc per FR-020.
assumptionReview.rationale: Verified by direct spot-read: parseMultipartRelated has @param×2 + @returns + @throws ×7 + @example at parse-multipart-related.ts:137-178; fetchAndHandleMultipart has @param×2 + @returns + @throws ×6 + @example at fetch-and-handle-multipart.ts:64-101; streamToString has @param×3 + @returns + @throws ×2 + @example ×2 at stream-helpers.ts:42-66; MultipartIdleTimeoutError has class-level description + @example + per-property doc + @param on constructor at errors.ts:18-46; src/index.ts re-exports the 12 public symbols (5 functions + 7 error classes) + 7 type aliases (Logger/MultipartFetchResult/MultipartHandlerOptions/ParseMultipartOptions/PartParser/ProgressSnapshot/StreamingMultipartPart). The audit is genuinely zero-source-change — the prior sprints landed the JSDoc per their respective contracts. ACCEPTABLE.

assumptionReview.assumption: T-082 verifies err.name within the CJS bundle, not via a real cross-bundle instanceof miss (which would require loading both ESM and CJS bundles in the same process).
assumptionReview.rationale: Verified at cross-format.test.ts:184-266 — the test constructs all 7 error classes from the CJS bundle and asserts `err.name === '<class-name>'` literal verbatim per NFR-DR-D-007. The contract per NFR-DR-D-007 is that the `name` discriminator is the class name verbatim (which is the actual cross-format fallback every consumer uses); spinning up a hybrid ESM+CJS process to trigger a real `instanceof` miss would test runtime ESM/CJS interop more than the library contract. The README at lines 179-212 documents the cross-format recipe with classifyByName(); the test verifies the underlying invariant (`err.name === <class-name>`) holds in the published CJS artifact. A future regression that set err.name to something else (e.g., parent Error's default 'Error') would fail this test immediately. ACCEPTABLE.

assumptionReview.assumption: Cross-format test uses inline runner-script strings written to per-test mkdtemp dirs, not pre-built fixture files.
assumptionReview.rationale: Verified at cross-format.test.ts:42-73 (runChild helper) — script content lives next to the assertions that verify its output, which is the most legible shape. mkdtemp + writeFile + spawn + cleanup-in-finally pattern is self-contained. Avoids a separate fixture tree that would need its own ESLint exemptions for being non-vitest .cjs/.mjs files. ACCEPTABLE.
